incidents.title: Rust crates arrayref, internment, append-only-vec compromised with build-time credential stealer
incidents.summary: A compromised maintainer account pushed malicious releases of three widely-used Rust crates — arrayref (245M+ total downloads, 403 dependents), internment, and append-only-vec — alongside a typosquat of proc-macro2. The build script downloads and runs a remote payload during compilation with no function call required, disables TLS validation, steals Chrome/Brave/Edge browser credentials, and installs OS-appropriate persistence (Registry, LaunchAgent, systemd). Nextron Systems caught it 07:15 UTC Aug 20; all three crates were pulled within 86-107 minutes, and researchers noted infrastructure overlap with prior North Korea-linked npm supply-chain operations. Durable catch: HTTPS POST beacons to /49890878 or any host resolving hwsrv-798836[.]hostwindsdns[.]com — that traffic means the build-time implant ran, regardless of which crate pulled it in.
incidents.action: Search ~/.cargo/registry/cache for deleted crate files matching arrayref 0.3.10, internment 0.8.7, or append-only-vec 0.1.9; pin arrayref to 0.3.9 or earlier (no patched version exists, no CVE assigned); rotate browser-stored credentials on any build host that compiled these crates between Aug 20 07:15-09:02 UTC; block hwsrv-798836[.]hostwindsdns[.]com and the payload/C2 IP.

iocs.context: Compromised releases with build-time credential-stealing implant
Additional malicious crate from the same campaign

incidents.title: CVE-2025-62593 — Ray framework DNS-rebinding RCE, now KEV-listed and tied to crypto-mining botnets
incidents.summary: Ray's job-submission endpoints (/api/jobs, /api/job_agent/jobs/) ship with no authentication by default. Attackers use DNS rebinding — a crafted website or ad that rebinds a domain to a victim's local or network-adjacent IP after passing a same-origin check — to make a developer's own browser submit malicious jobs to any reachable Ray instance. CISA added it to KEV Aug 17; the RondoDox DDoS botnet had already incorporated it two days before public disclosure, and the ongoing ShadowRay 2.0 campaign uses it to plant crypto-mining botnets on GPU clusters. Durable catch: any unauthenticated POST to a Ray cluster's /api/jobs or /api/job_agent/jobs/ endpoint from an unexpected origin — Ray was never meant to be reachable without a job submission client.
incidents.action: Upgrade Ray to 2.52.0 or later; never expose Ray dashboard/job endpoints directly to developer workstations or the internet — bind to localhost or place behind an authenticated proxy; audit GPU clusters for unexpected mining processes as a compromise indicator even after patching.

iocs.context: Ray framework unauthenticated job-endpoint RCE via DNS rebinding
Fixed version; FCEB deadline Aug 20

iocs.value: Unauthenticated request to /api/jobs or /api/job_agent/jobs/ from an unexpected browser origin

incidents.title: CVE-2026-33824 — Windows IKE Extension double-free RCE, actively exploited
incidents.summary: A double-free (CWE-415) in the Windows IKE and AuthIP Keying Modules service lets an unauthenticated remote attacker achieve code execution by sending malformed IKEv2 fragments to UDP port 500 or 4500 on any Windows 10, Windows 11, or Windows Server host with IKE enabled — no user interaction required. Microsoft shipped the fix in April 2026; CISA confirmed active exploitation and added it to KEV Aug 18 with a 3-day federal remediation deadline. Durable catch: inbound UDP/500 or UDP/4500 traffic from outside your expected IPsec peer set — Ray-style scanning of these ports for unpatched IKE Extension hosts is the precursor to exploitation.
facts: UDP 500/4500 · WORMABLE ACROSS ALL SUPPORTED WINDOWS
incidents.action: Apply Microsoft's April 2026 security update immediately if not already deployed; block inbound UDP/500 and UDP/4500 at the perimeter for hosts that don't use IKE; restrict remaining IKE traffic to known peer IP addresses via firewall rule.

iocs.context: Windows IKE/AuthIP double-free — unauth RCE via crafted IKEv2 fragments

iocs.value: Unexpected inbound UDP/500 or UDP/4500 traffic outside known IPsec peers
iocs.context: Precursor/exploitation traffic pattern

iocs.value: Microsoft April 2026 security update (KEV due date Aug 21)
iocs.context: Fix for CVE-2026-33824

incidents.title: CVE-2026-19478 — Critical GitLab GraphQL flaw lets unauthenticated attackers delete projects, exploited within minutes
incidents.summary: A code-injection flaw in a GitLab GraphQL directive lets an unauthenticated remote attacker modify or delete public projects and user data with no victim interaction — the third major GraphQL-layer vulnerability GitLab has patched in 2026. GitLab shipped an out-of-cycle emergency patch Aug 17; WatchTowr reproduced the exploit within minutes of disclosure, and its honeypot network caught the first in-the-wild attempts shortly after. Only self-managed instances are exposed — GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated were already patched. Durable catch: GraphQL mutation calls against public project/user endpoints from unauthenticated sessions — GitLab's normal API access pattern never looks like this.
facts: 3RD GRAPHQL-LAYER CVE IN GITLAB THIS YEAR
incidents.action: Patch self-managed GitLab to 19.2.4 / 19.1.6 / 19.0.8 / 18.11.11 immediately (GitLab.com/Dedicated already fixed); review GraphQL access logs for unauthenticated mutation calls against project-delete or user-data paths since Aug 17; restore any unexpectedly-deleted public project from backup.

iocs.context: GitLab GraphQL directive code injection — unauth project delete/modify
Out-of-cycle emergency patch, Aug 17

iocs.value: Unauthenticated GraphQL mutation requests against public project or user-data endpoints
iocs.context: In-the-wild exploitation pattern caught by WatchTowr honeypots

incidents.title: CVE-2026-73570 — Zimbra Collaboration SNMP command injection, actively exploited
incidents.summary: An OS command-injection flaw in Zimbra's SNMP monitoring path lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run arbitrary commands as the zimbra user, on any deployment with SNMP trap notifications (snmp_notify) and the swatchdog watchdog service enabled — swatchdog runs by default wherever zimbra-snmp is installed. Zimbra fixed it in 10.1.20 on Jul 20; CERT Polska's Alert 145/2026 (Aug 17) confirmed active in-the-wild exploitation against unpatched instances. Durable catch: the Zimbra service restarting without an admin-initiated cause, paired with new files under /opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps/, /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/, or /tmp/ owned by the zimbra user.
facts: FIXED JUL 20 · EXPLOITED IN WILD BY AUG 17
incidents.action: Patch Zimbra Collaboration Suite to 10.1.20 or later immediately; if you cannot patch, disable snmp_notify and stop the swatchdog service; review logs for unexplained Zimbra service restarts and new files under the jetty webapps/ or /tmp/ paths created by the zimbra user over the last 30 days.

iocs.context: Zimbra SNMP OS command injection — unauth RCE as zimbra user
Fixed release, Jul 20 2026

iocs.value: Unexplained Zimbra service restart; new files under /opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps/, /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/, or /tmp/ owned by zimbra
iocs.context: Exploitation and post-compromise signature per CERT Polska

incidents.title: Operation CameraSwarm — 14,500+ Dahua IP cameras compromised via credential attacks and P2P relay abuse
incidents.summary: A Russian-speaking, unattributed operator compromised 14,530+ Dahua IP camera IPs between Jun 17-Jul 22 using three converging techniques: direct credential attacks against 12,324 IPs, two-year-old authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2021-33044, CVE-2021-33045) to configure 1,923 cameras with persistent accounts, and abuse of Dahua's Easy4IP P2P relay infrastructure to reach 283 NAT-protected devices with no prior authentication at all. Both 2021 auth-bypass CVEs remain in CISA's KEV catalog. Durable catch: any Dahua device account creation or config change coming through the Easy4IP P2P relay path rather than direct admin access — that channel bypasses authentication entirely.
facts: 1,923 PERSISTENT ACCOUNTS · 283 VIA P2P RELAY (NO AUTH)
incidents.action: Install Dahua's repair software or the latest firmware from official channels; disable P2P/Easy4IP where not required; restrict remaining Easy4IP connectivity; replace default/weak credentials fleet-wide; segment surveillance networks from the rest of the environment.

iocs.context: Dahua NetKeyboard and loopback-login authentication bypass, still KEV-listed
Privilege escalation requiring existing credentials, used post-compromise

incidents.title: Threat actor "Satanic" leaks live Stripe merchant API keys and customer data for hundreds of accounts
incidents.summary: A threat actor using the handle "Satanic" uploaded roughly 35GB of Stripe merchant data to the cybercrime forum PwnForums on Aug 18 — 1,033 live API keys across 669 merchant account folders, exposing 1,350,336 unique customer emails and 688,000 customer records with names, phone numbers, and IP addresses. Stripe's own platform was not breached; the keys belong to individual merchants, likely harvested from exposed code, misconfigured environments, or prior infostealer logs. Satanic told Hudson Rock researchers this dump is a fraction of a claimed 20,000-key haul and threatened further releases. Durable catch: any Stripe API key that appears in a public repo, CI log, or infostealer dump should be treated as burned the moment it's found — rotation, not monitoring, is the only real fix.
incidents.action: Audit your Stripe account for API keys ever committed to a public repo, logged in CI output, or present on a developer machine previously infected by an infostealer, and rotate them now regardless of whether you appear in this specific dump; enable Stripe's restricted-key scoping so a leaked key can't fully drain an account.

iocs.context: Cybercrime forum post distributing the leaked Stripe merchant dataset

iocs.value: 1,033 live Stripe API keys across 669 merchant account folders (~35GB)
iocs.context: Scope of the initial public release

incidents.title: CVE-2026-32475 — Elementor Pro File Upload flaw lets unauthenticated attackers plant PHP web shells
incidents.summary: Elementor Pro's Forms module validates a file's extension and moves it to disk in two separate loops that handle empty file entries differently — submitting two file parts for the same upload field lets an unauthenticated attacker slip past the extension blocklist entirely and write a live PHP file straight into the public uploads directory. Any site with a published page containing a Form widget with a File Upload field is exposed, which Patchstack calls "an extremely common, everyday configuration." Elementor shipped 4.2.2 on Aug 19, one day before Wordfence/Patchstack detail went public. Durable catch: any .php file appearing under wp-content/uploads/elementor/forms/ — that path should never contain executable code.
facts: REQUIRES ONLY: A PUBLISHED FORM WIDGET WITH FILE UPLOAD
incidents.action: Update Elementor Pro to 4.2.2 or later immediately on every site running a Form widget with File Upload enabled; scan wp-content/uploads/elementor/forms/ for any .php (or double-extension) files and remove them; review server access logs for POST requests with duplicate file-part uploads to the same field.

iocs.context: Elementor Pro Forms File Upload extension-check bypass — unauth PHP write
Fixed release for all versions through 4.2.1
Web shell drop path from successful exploitation

incidents.title: Evooo1Bot — Mirai-derived botnet with encrypted C2 and SOCKS5 proxy relay hits routers and IoT devices
incidents.summary: A previously undocumented Linux botnet built on Mirai's DDoS engine, active since July 2026 and disclosed by FortiGuard Labs Aug 18. It chains 18 known CVEs across Alcatel OmniPCX, NETGEAR, D-Link, and Tenda devices for initial access, brute-forces SSH, intercepts HTTP Basic Auth credentials and cookies, and offers operators a SOCKS5 proxy relay on port 1080 alongside DNS/TCP/UDP DDoS capability — all coordinated over encrypted C2 on port 443 to blend with normal HTTPS traffic. Durable catch: unexpected SOCKS5 relay traffic on port 1080 from an IoT/router device, or that device making outbound port-443 connections it has no legitimate reason to make.
incidents.action: Patch firmware on routers/IoT devices against the 18 targeted CVEs (including CVE-2016-6277, CVE-2020-10987, CVE-2022-37055); replace default SSH credentials fleet-wide; monitor port 1080 for unexpected SOCKS5 activity and block unauthorized port-443 C2 traffic from IoT segments; inspect HTTP traffic for signs of Basic Auth/cookie interception.

iocs.context: Hardcoded string "evooo1"; combines DDoS, SSH brute-force, SOCKS5 relay, HTTP credential theft

incidents.title: InterLock ransomware publishes 710GB from Southeastern Oklahoma State University, 90,000+ students affected
incidents.summary: InterLock published its claimed haul from the July 31 attack on Southeastern Oklahoma State University on Aug 19 — 710GB covering more than 90,000 students' records (SSNs, grades, financial aid, disciplinary and medical information under FERPA/HIPAA protection) plus employee personal and injury data. The university's Durant campus closed for three days during initial containment; normal operations had resumed by Aug 18, one day before the leak-site publication. Durable catch: a ransomware group's leak-site publication date is a distinct, actionable event from the intrusion date — breach-notification and regulatory clocks (FERPA/HIPAA) often start running from disclosure, not from initial compromise.
incidents.action: Educational and healthcare-adjacent institutions should treat InterLock as an active threat to FERPA/HIPAA-covered data; verify backup integrity and segmentation between student-records systems and general campus IT; if you were a Southeastern Oklahoma State student or employee, monitor for identity-theft attempts given the SSN/medical data exposure.

iocs.context: Group's data-leak site publication of the stolen dataset

iocs.value: 710GB dataset spanning student and employee records (SSN, medical, financial aid)
iocs.context: Scope of published data per InterLock's claim
